page: Microsoft Azure E48pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 48-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the arm64 architecture, this server features dedicated CPU allocation with one thread per core, 128 MB of L3 cache, and 384 GB of RAM, translating to 8 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2835 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the E48pds_v6 demonstrates top-tier memory performance, achieving a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 463.82 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 199.65 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21816.0 and a Passmark database operations score of 37978.53, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-core performance and large-model LLM prompt processing represent relative tradeoffs, with the latter falling into the bottom 25% at 6.9 tokens/sec for a 70B model.

The ARM-based architecture provides high resource density, offering a cost-effective alternative to traditional x86 memory-optimized instances for memory-bound workloads. Given its high memory bandwidth, substantial local NVMe storage, and strong database operation benchmarks, the E48pds_v6 is highly suited for relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput redis caching layers, and large-scale data compilation tasks.
